playlist.name: Johann Sebastian Bach Essentials
playlist.description: Johann Sebastian Bach (1685-1750) is one of classical music's towering figures. A major composer of the Baroque era, Bach wrote hundreds of works for large ensembles (like the well-known Brandenburg Suites), solo instruments (including his famous suites for solo cello, numerous solo organ pieces, and the 'Goldberg Variations' for piano), oratorios and cantatas. Widely credited with furthering the German style of composition of the era, his music contains masterfully complex counterpoint. He was also an accomplished organist, and led the musical activities of several churches throughout his life, including in Köthen and Leipzig. In this playlist, you'll hear just a very small selection of important works written by Bach. (Cover: public domain)

playlist.name: Yo-Yo Ma Essentials
playlist.description: Yo-Yo Ma – one of the world’s most recognizable classical musicians – was born in 1955 to Chinese parents living in Paris. He began to study the cello with his father at age four and soon came with his family to New York, where he spent most of his formative years. He has performed for eight American presidents, including at the invitation of President Obama on the occasion of the 56th Inaugural Ceremony. Ma’s discography of over 100 albums reflects his wide-ranging interests, and he remains one of the best-selling recording artists in the classical field. In this playlist, get just a taste of the boundless musicality of Yo-Yo Ma. (Photo: Sony Masterworks, press)

playlist.name: Gabriel Schwabe Essentials
playlist.description: In this playlist, explore the discography of cellist Gabriel Schwabe (b. 1988), with music by Prokofiev, Brahms, Schumann, Kodály, and more. (Photo: Naxos)

playlist.name: Sheku Kanneh-Mason Essentials
playlist.description: Sheku Kanneh-Mason (b. 1999) has quickly become a household name since his breakout performance at the 2018 wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, where millions of people heard the deep expressivity and beautiful tone his playing possesses. The winner of the BBC's Young Musician Competition in 2016 – the first Black musician to win the prize – Kanneh-Mason has released chart-topping albums and performed as a soloist with the world's major orchestras, including the New York Philharmonic, the BBC Symphony, the NDR Elbphilharmonie Orchestra, and the Baltimore Symphony, among many others. In this playlist, explore his warm, masterful recordings of classic works, including the mighty Elgar Cello Concerto, as well as arrangements of well-loved tunes, from Bob Marley to Leonard Cohen to Welsh folk songs. (Photo: Decca Classics, press)
